transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-05
Start time (UTC): 16:00
Duration: 48 min
Attendees: Marcus Chen (Redwood AE), Leah Gomez (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Aisha Rahman (Novus - Procurement), Ben Wallace (Novus - Security), Priyanka Mehra (Novus - Legal), Dylan Ortiz (Novus - Platform)

Summary: Initial procurement / legal intake to align MSA/DPA exceptions, SLA requirements for a hybrid deployment (hosted + dedicated reserved capacity), and pricing approval workflow. Customer emphasized strict data residency and KMS/HSM controls for PHI-like data flows. Action items and next steps captured at the end.

Topics: MSA redlines, DPA clauses, SLA SLOs (p99 latency/uptime), pricing thresholds for reserved capacity, VPC / Private deployment options, SOC2/ISO evidence, SSO/SAML, KMS integrations, procurement approval path.

-- Transcript body (periodic timestamps, note: auto-transcript imperfect) --
00:00:12 Marcus Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call from our side, Leah and Samir are with me. Marcus for Redwood.
00:00:21 Aisha Rahman: Thanks Marcus. I'm Aisha, head of procurement. Ben our security lead's on. Priyanka from legal.
00:00:29 Ben Wallace: Hey all.
00:00:31 Leah Gomez: Hi, thanks. I'll do the technical bits and Samir will cover the Dedicated sizing and the benchmark plan.
00:00:40 Marcus Chen: Great. The purpose here is to map out the procurement path — MSA and DPA expectations, any SLA or exception items, and get aligned on what artifacts we need to hand off for approvals. Also to see whether you want Hosted first or go straight to Dedicated/Private.
00:01:05 Priyanka Mehra: From legal, we're mainly focused on data processing terms, breach notification timelines, indemnity carve-outs, and clarity on sub-processors. Also residency: for some workloads we need EU-only data handling.
00:01:22 Marcus Chen: Understood. On residency we have Private deploy options — VPC and on-prem — and Dedicated capacity in region. We can provide region controls and KMS integration.
00:01:36 Ben Wallace: Quick thing on KMS — we need HSM-backed keys, bring-your-own-key preferably. Also audit logs with token-level traces for 13 months. Is that covered?
00:01:50 Samir Patel: Yes, BYOK via KMS/HSM is supported on the Private package; we can also offer customer-managed keys for Dedicated in most cloud regions. Audit logs can be exported to your SIEM — we usually push to S3/secure bucket or direct to Splunk. We'll send the logging retention options.
00:02:10 Aisha Rahman: For procurement, our PO threshold is $250k for self-service, anything above goes to the sourcing committee. We likely will need a pricing approval path. How do you usually handle committed reserved capacity contracts?
00:02:26 Marcus Chen: We have reserved capacity contracts (Dedicated) with monthly or annual commits. We can provide term-based discounts. We'll send a sample pricing worksheet — Leah will share scenarios: 6-month pilot vs 12-month commit.
00:02:41 Dylan Ortiz: Operational question — if we start hosted, can we later migrate to Dedicated without disrupting keys or routing policies?
00:02:50 Leah Gomez: Yep, migration paths are supported. You can pin model versions and route traffic; there's an export for KV-cache state for warmup. Note: I said K-V cash earlier on another call — it's K-V cache — transcriptions sometimes say cash.
00:03:05 Priyanka Mehra: On the MSA, we have standard privacy/data clauses. One area of pushback will be breach notification timeline — our policy wants notice within 72 hours. What's Redwood's standard?
00:03:18 Marcus Chen: Our standard is 72 hours for unauthorized access, but we can discuss contractual language. We'll note that as a redline point.
00:03:27 Ben Wallace: Also SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001 certificate availability?
00:03:32 Samir Patel: We can provide SOC2 Type II report and ISO cert snapshots under NDA. We also have penetration test summaries. We'll attach those in the security pack.
00:03:45 Aisha Rahman: Good. Regarding DPA, we need subprocessor list and subprocessors' locations.
00:03:52 Marcus Chen: We'll provide the subprocessors list; it's in the security pack and in the DPA exhibit. Note: some auto-transcripts mem the word 'subprossor' — but it's subprocessor.
00:04:05 Priyanka Mehra: We may ask for an addendum that limits subprocessors to specific regions for EU data.
00:04:13 Leah Gomez: Technically doable if you use Private or Dedicated pinned to EU regions; hosted may still use multi-region infra for availability unless you opt for region pinning.
00:04:26 Ben Wallace: Latency and SLOs — our app requires 99th percentile under 250ms for short form prompts, and availability 99.95. Can you commit?
00:04:38 Marcus Chen: For Hosted our SLA is generally 99.9 for availability; Dedicated can get to 99.95 with commit + health check instrumentation. For p99 latency that depends on model and sequence lengths — Leah can run a model-profile with your typical payload. We usually avoid hard-coded p99 latency in MSAs except with Dedicated where we can set targets.
00:04:59 Leah Gomez: If you pick a quantized model and reserved GPU with the right kernel selection, p99 200-300ms is achievable for smaller contexts. For larger context windows it goes up. We'll run benchmarks against your sample prompts.
00:05:16 Aisha Rahman: Procurement needs pricing scenarios clear: pilot pricing, enterprise committed rate, early termination clauses. Also legal needs to know SLA credits mechanism.
00:05:27 Marcus Chen: We'll include an SLA credits section sample, and Leah will provide a pricing scenarios spreadsheet with termination terms and exit playbook.
00:05:37 Priyanka Mehra: On indemnity and liability caps — we'll likely request liability caps tied to fees. Is Redwood flexible?
00:05:45 Marcus Chen: We can discuss standard liability language; some changes may need legal review but we try to keep to market terms.
00:05:51 Ben Wallace: One more question: Do you support SAML SSO with Okta? We need RBAC integration and SCIM user provisioning.
00:05:59 Samir Patel: Yes, SAML SSO and SCIM are supported for console/console admin flows. For API keys and token management there are token-level RBAC features; we'll detail roles.
00:06:11 Dylan Ortiz: When you say token-level costs and tracing, can that be exported? We need cost attribution per team.
00:06:18 Leah Gomez: Yes console exposes token-level token-level cost breakdown per route. It can be exported via CSV or fed into the billing API.
00:06:25 Aisha Rahman: Procurement question: who signs the MSA at Redwood? VP Legal? Or VP Business? We need contact for counter-signer.
00:06:34 Marcus Chen: The legal team approves redlines; final signature typically by VP of Finance or CEO depending on contract size. We can provide standard signatory schedule.
00:06:44 Priyanka Mehra: We'll go through procurement gate steps: procurement intake -> security review -> legal redlines -> sourcing committee if over threshold. Can you list which docs to upload to our internal portal?
00:06:56 Marcus Chen: Yes: 1) Master Service Agreement (MSA) sample 2) Data Processing Agreement (DPA) with subprocessor list 3) SOC2/ISO/pen test summary 4) Pricing scenario worksheet 5) SLA exhibit 6) Security pack (redwood_security_pack_v3.pdf). I'll upload those.
00:07:15 Ben Wallace: A side note: we may ask for a contractual right to run an independent pen test on the Dedicated nodes. Is that allowed?
00:07:24 Samir Patel: For Dedicated we can carve out a controlled testing window and scope. For Hosted there are restrictions. We'll detail the pen test process and approvals.
00:07:35 Aisha Rahman: Timeline — procurement wants contract signed by end of October. That gives us about 7 weeks. Is that realistic?
00:07:43 Marcus Chen: Yes, if we get redlines within a week and set up a pilot quickly we can hit that target. We'll need your procurement and legal deliverables by 2025-09-12 to keep momentum.
00:07:56 Priyanka Mehra: We'll review MSA/DPA and give initial redlines. Please flag any non-negotiables upfront.
00:08:04 Marcus Chen: We'll mark must-haves in the DPA and MSA and call out negotiable items.
00:08:10 Leah Gomez: Operationally, for the technical benchmark we need a dataset of sample prompts, expected throughput, and peak concurrencies. Also network egress constraints if any.
00:08:20 Dylan Ortiz: We'll provide sample prompts and expected concurrency chart. Does Redwood support VPC peering or PrivateLink for low-latency egress?
00:08:29 Samir Patel: We support VPC peering, PrivateLink and direct connect options depending on cloud provider. For on-prem we have an appliance pattern.
00:08:40 Ben Wallace: Competitors question — our security folks also evaluated Anthropic and ManagedCloudAI. How do you compare on contractual transparency and data controls?
00:08:50 Marcus Chen: We try to be very explicit: regional pinning, BYOK, dedicated pools, and transparent kernel/quantization profiles. We'll surface those differentiators in the security pack.
00:09:02 Aisha Rahman: Any immediate blockers for procurement to start legal review?
00:09:07 Priyanka Mehra: We need the MSA and DPA and a subprocessors list. Also sample SLA exhibit for Dedicated.
00:09:13 Marcus Chen: We'll deliver those today.
00:09:17 Leah Gomez: We'll also share the Dedicated sizing/price estimator and a short tech note on performance expectations.
00:09:24 Marcus Chen: Ok let's capture action items.
00:09:28 -- end of technical discussion, capture action items and close --
00:09:30 Marcus Chen: Recap: Marcus to send DPA + security pack; Leah to share pricing scenarios and sizing worksheet; Samir to schedule benchmark window; Novus to provide PO threshold confirmation and provide Okta SAML metadata and sample prompts.
00:09:48 Aisha Rahman: Sounds good. We'll aim to get procurement's gating doc to you by Friday 2025-09-12.
00:09:56 Priyanka Mehra: We'll send legal redlines within the week.
00:10:02 Marcus Chen: Great. Anything else?
00:10:05 Dylan Ortiz: No, that's it. Thanks everyone.
00:10:08 Marcus Chen: Thanks. We'll follow up with the packet and next meeting invite for the benchmark week.

Note: transcript contains small transcription artifacts (misspelled proper nouns, partial words) consistent with auto-transcription. Shared artifacts referenced during call: redwood_security_pack_v3.pdf, pricing_sheet_estimate.xlsx, Dedicated_sizing_worksheet.xlsx.
